// kineticql

One query language for all three signals

If you can read the query, you can read the incident. KineticQL is SQL with three additions and no hidden rewriting.

  • Joins across traces, metrics and logs in one statement
  • Every dashboard panel shows the query that produced it
  • Saved queries are files, versioned beside the service they watch
Open the language reference
slo/checkout.kql 
select percentile(duration, 0.99) as p99,
       count_if(status = "error") as errors
from spans
join logs using (trace_id)
where service = "checkout"
group by bucket(ts, "1m")

// questions

Asked often enough to answer here

Do I have to install a proprietary agent? +

No. The ingest endpoint speaks OpenTelemetry, and the collector we publish is the upstream one with a configuration file.

What happens when I exceed the plan volume? +

Ingest keeps working and the overage is billed per gigabyte at the published rate. Nothing is dropped and nothing is sampled without you asking for it.

Can I get my data out? +

A full Parquet export is available on every plan, at any point, at no charge. Export is not a retention feature, it is a right.

Is the self-hosted build the same code? +

Same binary, same release tag. The difference is where the object store lives and who holds the keys.

Still holding a question?

A support engineer answers in the same channel you write in, and there is no tier that buys you a faster human.

Talk to support

Why we price on bytes

Engineering note

Series-based pricing asks an engineer to guess, at instrumentation time, which label will matter during an incident that has not happened yet. That guess is always wrong, and the cost of being wrong is paid at the worst possible moment.

A pricing model is a design decision. Ours says: label everything, and find out later what mattered.

Bytes are a number both sides can measure, and they move in the direction engineers can actually control: sampling, retention, and what is worth keeping hot.

Noor Sahel, Reliability
